title: Abstract classes without abstract methods
answer: Yes. An abstract class may contain zero abstract methods. Declaring the class abstract can still prevent direct instantiation and signal that the type exists only as a shared base for subclasses. This is sometimes useful for controlled construction or framework design, although composition or a concrete base should be considered when subclassing is not actually required.
